title: Simple chamber folding rewrites an affine lowering edge in at most two edges
statement:
Let $X$ be a free abelian group of finite rank (a $\mathbf Z$-module with a finite basis) [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Let $\Phi\subset X\setminus\{0\}$ be finite with $\Phi\cap\mathbf Q\beta=\{\beta,-\beta\}$ for $\beta\in\Phi$. For every $\beta\in\Phi$ let $c_\beta:X\to\mathbf Z$ be a homomorphism, with $c_\beta(\beta)=2$ and $c_{-\beta}=-c_\beta$. Set $s_\beta(v)=v-c_\beta(v)\beta$. Assume $s_\beta(\Phi)=\Phi$ and $c_{s_\beta\gamma}=c_\gamma\circ s_\beta$ for all roots $\beta,\gamma$. Let $\Delta\subset\Phi$ be linearly independent in $X\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, with every root an integral combination of $\Delta$ whose coefficients are all nonnegative or all nonpositive. Let $\Phi^+$ be the roots of the first kind. Fix any $\rho\in X$ and integer $p\ge1$. Put $s_\beta\mathbin\cdot v=s_\beta(v+\rho)-\rho$, and write $u\le v$ when $v-u$ is an integral nonnegative sum of $\Delta$. An affine lowering edge from $v$ to $u$ means
$$u=s_\beta\mathbin\cdot v+np\beta\le v\quad(\beta\in\Phi^+,\ n\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}).$$
For $\alpha\in\Delta$ define
$f_\alpha(v)=v$ if $c_\alpha(v+\rho)\ge0$, and $f_\alpha(v)=s_\alpha\mathbin\cdot v$ otherwise.
For every affine lowering edge from $v$ to $u$ there is a sequence $f_\alpha(v)=t_0,t_1,\ldots,t_m=f_\alpha(u)$ with $0\le m\le2$, each $t_{j-1}\to t_j$ an affine lowering edge. Equality of the folded endpoints permits $m=0$. No irreducibility assumption or primality assumption on $p$ is imposed.

proof.text: Work with shifted coordinates $x=v+\rho$, $y=u+\rho$; translation back by $-\rho$ preserves every difference. In these coordinates put $R_{\delta,j}(z)=s_\delta z+jp\delta=z-(c_\delta(z)-jp)\delta$ and $F(z)=z$ for $c_\alpha(z)\ge0$, $F(z)=s_\alpha z$ otherwise. The given edge is $y=R_{\beta,n}(x)=x-k\beta$, where $k=c_\beta(x)-np$. We have $k\ge0$: write $\beta=\sum d_\delta\delta$ with $d_\delta\ge0$ and some $d_\delta>0$; the hypothesis $y\le x$ and independence of $\Delta$ force the coefficients $kd_\delta$ of $x-y$ to be nonnegative. These coefficient comparisons may be made in $X\otimes\mathbf Q$: a basis as defined in [def-weil-pbc-free-module] identifies $X$ with a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathbf Z$, so its map to that rational vector space is injective. Any displayed $R_{\delta,j}$ step below is therefore a lowering edge once $\delta\in\Phi^+$, $j\ge0$ and its subtraction coefficient is nonnegative.

proof.text: The identities $c_\alpha(s_\alpha z)=-c_\alpha(z)$ and $s_\alpha^2z=z$ follow by substituting $c_\alpha(\alpha)=2$. If $\beta\ne\alpha$, put $\gamma=s_\alpha\beta$. Then $\gamma\in\Phi^+$: some coefficient of $\beta$ away from $\alpha$ is positive (otherwise reducedness would give $\beta=\alpha$), and that coefficient is unchanged by $s_\alpha\beta=\beta-c_\alpha(\beta)\alpha$. Since $\gamma$ is a root and every root has coefficients of one sign, all its coefficients are nonnegative.

source.place: Definition 1 and Lemma 1, printed pp.54–55, local chamber-reduction prerequisite; explicit agent-written calculation (the PDF is absent locally; see report.md).

proof.text:
Still suppose $\beta\ne\alpha$. The assumed covariance gives $c_\gamma(s_\alpha x)=c_\beta(x)$, and direct substitution gives
$$s_\alpha y=s_\alpha x-k\gamma=R_{\gamma,n}(s_\alpha x).$$
Indeed $R_{\gamma,n}(s_\alpha x)=s_\alpha x-(c_\beta(x)-np)\gamma$, by $s_\alpha^2=1$. Thus $s_\alpha x\longrightarrow s_\alpha y$ is a lowering edge at the same level $n$, with subtraction coefficient $k\ge0$.

source.place: Definition 1 and Lemma 1, printed pp.54–55, local chamber-reduction prerequisite; explicit agent-written calculation (the PDF is absent locally; see report.md).

proof.text: Write $a=c_\alpha(x)$ and $b=c_\alpha(y)$, and assume $\beta\ne\alpha$. If $a,b\ge0$, use the original edge $F(x)=x\to y=F(y)$. If $a,b<0$, use the conjugated edge $F(x)=s_\alpha x\to s_\alpha y=F(y)$ from step 3. If $a<0\le b$, use $s_\alpha x\to x\to y$: the first edge is $R_{\alpha,0}(s_\alpha x)=x$ with subtraction coefficient $-a>0$, and the second is the original edge. These paths have at most two edges.

source.place: Definition 1 and Lemma 1, printed pp.54–55, local chamber-reduction prerequisite; explicit agent-written calculation (the PDF is absent locally; see report.md).

proof.text: In the remaining sign case for $\beta\ne\alpha$, namely $b<0\le a$, use $x\to s_\alpha x\to s_\alpha y$. The first edge is $R_{\alpha,0}(x)=s_\alpha x$ with coefficient $a\ge0$, and the second is precisely the conjugated edge of step 3 with root $\gamma\in\Phi^+$ and level $n\ge0$. Its endpoints are $F(x)$ and $F(y)$. This exhausts the cases with $\beta\ne\alpha$, including points on the wall.

source.place: Definition 1 and Lemma 1, printed pp.54–55, local chamber-reduction prerequisite; explicit agent-written calculation (the PDF is absent locally; see report.md).

proof.text:
It remains to treat $\beta=\alpha$. Here $k=a-np\ge0$, so $a\ge np\ge0$, and $b=c_\alpha(y)=-a+2np$. If $b\ge0$ the original edge already joins the folded endpoints. Suppose $b<0$, equivalently $a>2np$. Then
$$F(x)=x,\qquad F(y)=s_\alpha y=x-np\alpha.$$
For $n=0$ these are equal, so take the empty path. For $n\ge1$, divide $a$ by $p>0$: write $a=hp+r$ with integers $0\le r<p$. The inequality $a>2np$ forces $h\ge2n$ (if $h\le2n-1$ then $a<(h+1)p\le2np$). In particular $h\ge0$ and $h-n\ge0$.

source.place: Definition 1 and Lemma 1, printed pp.54–55, local chamber-reduction prerequisite; explicit agent-written calculation (the PDF is absent locally; see report.md).

proof.text:
For this last case let $z=x-r\alpha$. Substitution yields
$$z=R_{\alpha,h}(x),\qquad c_\alpha(z)=a-2r=hp-r,$$
so $x\to z$ is a lowering edge with coefficient $r\ge0$. A second substitution yields
$$R_{\alpha,h-n}(z)=z-\bigl((hp-r)-(h-n)p\bigr)\alpha=x-np\alpha=F(y).$$
Its coefficient is $np-r>0$, since $n\ge1$ and $r<p$, and its level is $h-n\ge0$. Thus $F(x)=x\to z\to F(y)$ is the required two-edge path. No divisibility of $a$ by $p$ was used.

source.place: Definition 1 and Lemma 1, printed pp.54–55, local chamber-reduction prerequisite; explicit agent-written calculation (the PDF is absent locally; see report.md).

proof.text: Translate each vertex back by $-\rho$. Since $F(v+\rho)-\rho=f_\alpha(v)$ and similarly for $u$, the paths above have exactly the required endpoints and edge formulas in the original coordinates. Remove any stationary edge (or take $m=0$ whenever the endpoints coincide); this leaves at most two edges. The construction uses only $p>0$ and the stated base and reflection hypotheses, not primality or irreducibility. If $\Phi$ or $\Delta$ is empty, there is no choice of $\alpha\in\Delta$ and the assertion is vacuous.
